title: DeviceInfo - Android and Wear OS device information
description: See the full specification of your Android phone and Wear OS watch: hardware, battery charge speed, sensors, cameras and network.
kicker: Android and Wear OS device information
h1: Read the full specification of your Android phone and Wear OS watch.
lead: DeviceInfo shows everything Android tells an app about the device it runs on: the system, the hardware and the processor, the display, the memory and storage, the battery with its charge speed, the sensors, the cameras and the network.
whatfor: It is for the moments when you need exact facts about a device: when you wonder what is really inside your phone, when you compare chargers, when you ask someone for help and have to describe your device.
scnTitle: What you can do with it
scn: See what is inside your phone
Model, build, processor, memory, storage, display and Android version, in grouped sections that fold and unfold. The groups stay the way you leave them.

The Battery section shows the charge speed in mA and watts, the power profile, the nominal profile, the estimated time to a full charge and the estimated runtime left. When a device does not expose a value, the report says so.
Describe your device to whoever helps you

Copy, save or share the whole report, or copy one section. Values that identify the device in a network - the signature hash, local addresses and mount paths - are hidden in the default copy and included only after you confirm.
Read your watch on your phone
On the watch, Send to phone hands its report to the paired phone, which stores it and shows a notification that opens or shares it.
Find out what sensors and cameras can do
Every sensor and every camera of the device is listed with its capabilities. The app takes no pictures and records no sound.
getIntro: One Google Play listing carries both apps, the phone app and the watch app.
steps: Install DeviceInfo from Google Play on your phone.
Open it. The report appears at once; tap the title of a group to fold or unfold it.
Use Copy, Save or Share in the toolbar for the whole report; one section can be copied on its own.
watchNote: On a Wear OS watch, open the same Google Play listing to install the watch app, then tap Send to phone. It needs the watch paired with the phone and Google Play services on both; on Android 13 and later the phone asks once for permission to show the notification.
featPhoneText: Grouped, collapsible sections of the device report.
featWatchText: Glanceable sections of the watch itself, and Send to phone.
featPrivText: No account, no server, no telemetry and no ads. Neither app has the internet permission, so what you see stays on the device unless you copy, save, share or send it yourself.
helpIntro: The developer answers messages personally; there is no support team and no guaranteed response time.
faq: A value says unknown, or the Battery section says the device does not expose it. Is something broken?
No. The report shows what the device reports about itself and never invents a figure; a value the device does not expose is shown as unknown.
Send to phone shows no notification on the phone.

On Android 13 and later the phone asks once for permission to show it. While notifications are off, the menu of the System information screen offers Turn on notifications. The phone keeps the report either way.
Send to phone does not reach the phone.
The link between the watch and the phone is the Wearable Data Layer of Google Play services, so the watch must be paired with the phone and both need Google Play services.
What does the default copy leave out?
The signature hash of the app, local network addresses and storage mount paths. Copying the full report asks you to confirm first.
Only through an action you choose: Copy, Save, Share, or Send to phone from the watch. Neither app has the internet permission.
tech: Phone app: Android 8.0 (API 26) or later. Watch app: Wear OS on Android 9 (API 28) or later.
Languages: English, Russian and Ukrainian, on the phone and on the watch.
Application id: com.sza.deviceinfo, one id for the phone app and the watch app.
Distribution: Google Play, phone and watch in one listing.
Permissions: network state and notifications on the phone, Wi-Fi state on the watch. Nothing else: no internet, location, contacts, storage, camera or microphone permission.
priv: The developer receives none of your data: there is no server, no account, and no analytics, crash reporting, advertising or tracking code.
Android backup is switched off for both apps, and everything the apps store is removed when you uninstall them.
Read the privacy policy in full.
Open source under the MIT License; the licenses of the components the apps are built from are listed in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt, shipped inside both packages.
